records.source: Βίβλος γενέσεως Ἰησοῦ χριστοῦ υἱοῦ Δαυὶδ υἱοῦ Ἀβραάμ.
records.gloss: Book of origin of Jesus Christ, son of David, son of Abraham.
pieces: The record of the family line of Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, the son of David, the son of Abraham.

L.1: [The] book of [the] origin of Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, son of David, son of Abraham.

R.1: This is a list of the ancestors of Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. He came from the family of King David, and from the family of Abraham.

decisions.choice: book of origin: a record of where Jesus came from, opening the family line of 1:2-17
alternatives: a heading for the whole Gospel ("the book of the history of Jesus")
decisions.reason: The word for origin is the one 1:18 uses for Jesus's birth, and in Genesis it heads lists of descendants (Genesis 5:1, in the Greek Old Testament). Here it heads the list that follows. Some read it as a title for the whole book, as if it said "a new Genesis"; the phrase can bear that, but the list it introduces is the plainest reference.

decisions.choice: an echo of Genesis 2:4 and 5:1, where the same phrase opens an account
decisions.reason: In the Greek Old Testament the same two words open the account of heaven and earth (Genesis 2:4) and the list of Adam's descendants (Genesis 5:1). Matthew's first words sound like the first book of Scripture.

decisions.choice: son of David, son of Abraham: Jesus as the heir of the promises made to both
decisions.reason: God promised David a son whose kingdom would last for ever (2 Samuel 7:12-16), and "son of David" became a way of speaking of the coming king (Matthew 9:27; 21:9). God promised Abraham that all nations would be blessed through his offspring (Genesis 12:3; 22:18). Both titles describe Jesus, not David.

decisions.choice: He came from the family of King David, and from the family of Abraham
alternatives: son of David, son of Abraham
decisions.reason: "Son" here means descendant; Readable says so, adds "King" so a new reader knows who David was, and makes it clear that both titles describe Jesus.

decisions.choice: the family line (B); a list of the ancestors (R)
decisions.reason: The record that follows is a family line, so Balanced and Readable name it that way. Literal keeps "origin", the word 1:18 repeats.

records.heading: The ancestors of Jesus

records.source: Ἀβραὰμ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰσαάκ, Ἰσαὰκ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰακώβ, Ἰακὼβ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰούδαν καὶ τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς αὐτοῦ, Ἰούδας δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Φαρὲς καὶ τὸν Ζάρα ἐκ τῆς Θαμάρ, Φαρὲς δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἑσρώμ, Ἑσρὼμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀράμ, Ἀρὰμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀμιναδάβ, Ἀμιναδὰβ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ναασσών, Ναασσὼν δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Σαλμών, Σαλμὼν δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Βόες ἐκ τῆς Ῥαχάβ, Βόες δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰωβὴδ ἐκ τῆς Ῥούθ, Ἰωβὴδ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰεσσαί, Ἰεσσαὶ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Δαυὶδ τὸν βασιλέα.
records.gloss: Abraham begat the Isaac, Isaac then begat the Jacob, Jacob then begat the Judah and the brothers of him, \v 3 Judah then begat the Perez and the Zerah out of the Tamar, Perez then begat the Hezron, Hezron then begat the Ram, \v 4 Ram then begat the Amminadab, Amminadab then begat the Nahshon, Nahshon then begat the Salmon, \v 5 Salmon then begat the Boaz out of the Rahab, Boaz then begat the Obed out of the Ruth, Obed then begat the Jesse, \v 6 Jesse then begat the David the king.
pieces: Abraham was the father of Isaac, Isaac of Jacob, and Jacob of Judah and his brothers.
Judah was the father of Perez and Zerah by Tamar. Perez was the father of Hezron, and Hezron of Ram.
Ram was the father of Amminadab, Amminadab of Nahshon, and Nahshon of Salmon.
Salmon was the father of Boaz by Rahab. Boaz was the father of Obed by Ruth. Obed was the father of Jesse,
and Jesse was the father of David the king.

L.2: Abraham fathered Isaac, and Isaac fathered Jacob, and Jacob fathered Judah and his brothers,
L.3: and Judah fathered Perez and Zerah by Tamar, and Perez fathered Hezron, and Hezron fathered Ram,
L.4: and Ram fathered Amminadab, and Amminadab fathered Nahshon, and Nahshon fathered Salmon,
L.5: and Salmon fathered Boaz by Rahab, and Boaz fathered Obed by Ruth, and Obed fathered Jesse,
L.6: and Jesse fathered David the king.

R.2: Abraham was the father of Isaac. Isaac was the father of Jacob. Jacob was the father of Judah and Judah's brothers.
R.3: Judah was the father of Perez and Zerah, and their mother was Tamar. Perez was the father of Hezron. Hezron was the father of Ram.
R.4: Ram was the father of Amminadab. Amminadab was the father of Nahshon. Nahshon was the father of Salmon.
R.5: Salmon was the father of Boaz, and Boaz's mother was Rahab. Boaz was the father of Obed, and Obed's mother was Ruth. Obed was the father of Jesse.
R.6: Jesse was the father of David, who became king.

decisions.choice: begat: was the father of, the link from one generation to the next
decisions.reason: The verb names a father's part in a birth. In a family line it can also link a man to a later descendant (see 1:8), but in this stretch each link matches the father-son lists of 1 Chronicles 2:1-15 and Ruth 4:18-22.

decisions.choice: Tamar, Rahab and Ruth: three women named in a list that normally names only men
alternatives: the mothers are named only for completeness
decisions.reason: Family lists of the time traced descent through fathers and seldom named mothers. Matthew names four women before Mary (Tamar, Rahab, Ruth, and Uriah's wife in 1:6). Each came into the line in an unusual way (Genesis 38; Joshua 2; Ruth 1-4; 2 Samuel 11), and at least Rahab, a Canaanite, and Ruth, a Moabite, were not Israelites. The text does not say why they are named. Their stories prepare for Mary's unusual pregnancy in 1:18, and the foreigners for the nations of 28:19.

decisions.choice: Rahab: the woman of Jericho who hid Israel's spies (Joshua 2; 6:25)
alternatives: another woman of the same name
decisions.reason: The Old Testament does not name Salmon's wife; Matthew is the only source that names her. No other Rahab appears in Scripture, and Hebrews 11:31 and James 2:25 also remember Rahab of Jericho.

decisions.choice: David the king: the title marks David as the turning point of the line
alternatives: a title with no special weight
decisions.reason: No one else in the list is given a title. The title closes the first of the three sets of fourteen (1:17) and points back to "son of David" in 1:1.

decisions.choice: fathered (L); was the father of (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek verb names the father's part in a birth. "Begot" is no longer current English. Balanced and Readable use the phrase people use when they talk about a family tree; Balanced lets later links in a run share one verb ("Isaac of Jacob").

decisions.choice: names in their Old Testament form: Perez, Hezron, Ram
alternatives: the Greek forms: Phares, Esrom, Aram
decisions.reason: Matthew spells the names as they were written in Greek. English readers know these people from the Old Testament (1 Chronicles 2:4-10; Ruth 4:18-22), so the names are given in their Old Testament form at every level.

decisions.choice: by Tamar (B); their mother was Tamar, Boaz's mother was Rahab (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek "out of" names the mother. Balanced uses "by", as English does when naming the mother in a family line; Readable says it in full.

records.source: Δαυὶδ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Σολομῶνα ἐκ τῆς τοῦ Οὐρίου, Σολομὼν δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ῥοβοάμ, Ῥοβοὰμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀβιά, Ἀβιὰ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀσάφ, Ἀσὰφ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰωσαφάτ, Ἰωσαφὰτ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰωράμ, Ἰωρὰμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ὀζίαν, Ὀζίας δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰωαθάμ, Ἰωαθὰμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀχάζ, Ἀχὰζ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἑζεκίαν, Ἑζεκίας δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Μανασσῆ, Μανασσῆς δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀμώς, Ἀμὼς δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰωσίαν, Ἰωσίας δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰεχονίαν καὶ τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τῆς μετοικεσίας Βαβυλῶνος.
records.gloss: David then begat the Solomon out of the [wife] of the Uriah, \v 7 Solomon then begat the Rehoboam, Rehoboam then begat the Abijah, Abijah then begat the Asaph, \v 8 Asaph then begat the Jehoshaphat, Jehoshaphat then begat the Joram, Joram then begat the Uzziah, \v 9 Uzziah then begat the Jotham, Jotham then begat the Ahaz, Ahaz then begat the Hezekiah, \v 10 Hezekiah then begat the Manasseh, Manasseh then begat the Amos, Amos then begat the Josiah, \v 11 Josiah then begat the Jechoniah and the brothers of him at the deportation of Babylon.
pieces: David was the father of Solomon by the wife of Uriah.
Solomon was the father of Rehoboam, Rehoboam of Abijah, and Abijah of Asa.
Asa was the father of Jehoshaphat, Jehoshaphat of Joram, and Joram of Uzziah.
Uzziah was the father of Jotham, Jotham of Ahaz, and Ahaz of Hezekiah.
Hezekiah was the father of Manasseh, Manasseh of Amon, and Amon of Josiah.
Josiah was the father of Jechoniah and his brothers at the time of the deportation to Babylon.

L.6: And David fathered Solomon by the [wife] of Uriah,
L.7: and Solomon fathered Rehoboam, and Rehoboam fathered Abijah, and Abijah fathered Asaph,
L.8: and Asaph fathered Jehoshaphat, and Jehoshaphat fathered Joram, and Joram fathered Uzziah,
L.9: and Uzziah fathered Jotham, and Jotham fathered Ahaz, and Ahaz fathered Hezekiah,
L.10: and Hezekiah fathered Manasseh, and Manasseh fathered Amos, and Amos fathered Josiah,
L.11: and Josiah fathered Jechoniah and his brothers at [the time of] the deportation to Babylon.

R.6: David was the father of Solomon, and Solomon's mother had been the wife of Uriah.
R.7: Solomon was the father of Rehoboam. Rehoboam was the father of Abijah. Abijah was the father of Asa.
R.8: Asa was the father of Jehoshaphat. Jehoshaphat was the father of Joram. Joram was the father of Uzziah.
R.9: Uzziah was the father of Jotham. Jotham was the father of Ahaz. Ahaz was the father of Hezekiah.
R.10: Hezekiah was the father of Manasseh. Manasseh was the father of Amon. Amon was the father of Josiah.
R.11: Josiah was the father of Jechoniah and his brothers. That was the time when the people of Judah were taken away to Babylon.

decisions.choice: the [wife] of Uriah: Bathsheba, named by her first husband
decisions.reason: The Greek says only "the [one] of Uriah"; the feminine article shows a woman is meant. She is Bathsheba, whom David took while she was Uriah's wife, and whose husband he had killed (2 Samuel 11-12). Calling her by Uriah's name keeps that story in view.

decisions.choice: Asaph and Amos, the reading of the SBLGNT, standing for the kings Asa and Amon
alternatives: Asa and Amon, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: The kings of Judah were Asa (1 Kings 15:9) and Amon (2 Kings 21:18). The SBLGNT follows early manuscripts that spell them Asaph, like the psalmist, and Amos, like the prophet; many later manuscripts have Asa and Amon. Whether Matthew used spellings current in his day or meant an echo of the psalmist and the prophet, the kings are meant either way. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Joram begat Uzziah: Uzziah was Joram's great-great-grandson
decisions.reason: Between Joram and Uzziah (also called Azariah) the books of Kings and Chronicles list three kings: Ahaziah, Joash and Amaziah (1 Chronicles 3:11-12). Family lists often left out generations, and the verb can link a man to a later descendant. The shorter list gives the fourteen of 1:17.

decisions.choice: Jechoniah: King Jehoiachin, Josiah's grandson, taken to Babylon in 597 BC
decisions.reason: Jechoniah is another name for Jehoiachin (1 Chronicles 3:16; Jeremiah 24:1), the son of Jehoiakim and grandson of Josiah. Nebuchadnezzar took him to Babylon (2 Kings 24:10-16). Here, too, a generation is passed over. "His brothers" may be his uncles, the other sons of Josiah who reigned (1 Chronicles 3:15), or his own brothers.

decisions.choice: the deportation to Babylon: the exile, when Judah's king and people were carried off
decisions.reason: The word means removal to a new place. It names the forced removal of Judah's king and leading people to Babylon in 597 BC and after the fall of Jerusalem in 586 BC (2 Kings 24-25).

decisions.choice: fathered (L); was the father of (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek verb names the father's part in a birth. "Begot" is no longer current English. Balanced and Readable use the phrase people use when they talk about a family tree; Balanced lets later links in a run share one verb ("Isaac of Jacob").

decisions.choice: Asaph and Amos (L); Asa and Amon (B, R)
alternatives: Asaph and Amos at every level
decisions.reason: The people are the same at every level. Literal keeps the spelling of the Greek text; Balanced and Readable use the names the kings have in the Old Testament, so that readers do not take them for the psalmist and the prophet. A footnote gives the Greek spelling (see the meaning note).

decisions.choice: That was the time when the people of Judah were taken away to Babylon
decisions.reason: Readable explains the event in its own sentence and says who was taken.

records.source: Μετὰ δὲ τὴν μετοικεσίαν Βαβυλῶνος Ἰεχονίας ἐγέννησεν τὸν Σαλαθιήλ, Σαλαθιὴλ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ζοροβαβέλ, Ζοροβαβὲλ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀβιούδ, Ἀβιοὺδ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἐλιακίμ, Ἐλιακὶμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀζώρ, Ἀζὼρ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Σαδώκ, Σαδὼκ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀχίμ, Ἀχὶμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἐλιούδ, Ἐλιοὺδ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἐλεάζαρ, Ἐλεάζαρ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ματθάν, Ματθὰν δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰακώβ, Ἰακὼβ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰωσὴφ τὸν ἄνδρα Μαρίας, ἐξ ἧς ἐγεννήθη Ἰησοῦς ὁ λεγόμενος χριστός.
records.gloss: After then the deportation of Babylon Jechoniah begat the Shealtiel, Shealtiel then begat the Zerubbabel, \v 13 Zerubbabel then begat the Abiud, Abiud then begat the Eliakim, Eliakim then begat the Azor, \v 14 Azor then begat the Zadok, Zadok then begat the Achim, Achim then begat the Eliud, \v 15 Eliud then begat the Eleazar, Eleazar then begat the Matthan, Matthan then begat the Jacob, \v 16 Jacob then begat the Joseph the husband of Mary, out of whom was begotten Jesus the [one] being called Christ.
pieces: After the deportation to Babylon, Jechoniah was the father of Shealtiel, and Shealtiel of Zerubbabel.
Zerubbabel was the father of Abiud, Abiud of Eliakim, and Eliakim of Azor.
Azor was the father of Zadok, Zadok of Achim, and Achim of Eliud.
Eliud was the father of Eleazar, Eleazar of Matthan, and Matthan of Jacob.
Jacob was the father of Joseph, the husband of Mary, and of Mary was born Jesus, who is called {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

L.12: And after the deportation to Babylon, Jechoniah fathered Shealtiel, and Shealtiel fathered Zerubbabel,
L.13: and Zerubbabel fathered Abiud, and Abiud fathered Eliakim, and Eliakim fathered Azor,
L.14: and Azor fathered Zadok, and Zadok fathered Achim, and Achim fathered Eliud,
L.15: and Eliud fathered Eleazar, and Eleazar fathered Matthan, and Matthan fathered Jacob,
L.16: and Jacob fathered Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, the [one] called {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.

R.12: After the people were taken to Babylon, Jechoniah was the father of Shealtiel. Shealtiel was the father of Zerubbabel.
R.13: Zerubbabel was the father of Abiud. Abiud was the father of Eliakim. Eliakim was the father of Azor.
R.14: Azor was the father of Zadok. Zadok was the father of Achim. Achim was the father of Eliud.
R.15: Eliud was the father of Eleazar. Eleazar was the father of Matthan. Matthan was the father of Jacob.
R.16: Jacob was the father of Joseph. Joseph was the husband of Mary, and Mary was the mother of Jesus, who is called {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

decisions.choice: of whom was born: Mary alone is the parent named, and the verb turns passive
alternatives: Joseph and Mary together as parents
decisions.reason: Every link so far has been "X fathered Y". At the last link the pattern breaks: "whom" is feminine, so it is Mary of whom Jesus was born, and the verb becomes "was born". Matthew does not say that Joseph fathered Jesus. Verses 18-25 explain why.

decisions.choice: Joseph the husband of Mary: the line runs through Joseph, Jesus's legal father
decisions.reason: The list traces Joseph's ancestors. A man who named and accepted a child as his own made the child his legal son (1:25), so Jesus is counted a son of David through Joseph, whom the angel calls "son of David" (1:20).

decisions.choice: Shealtiel and Zerubbabel are known from the Old Testament; the names after them are not
alternatives: all the names come from Old Testament lists
decisions.reason: Shealtiel and Zerubbabel lead the return from exile (Ezra 3:2; Haggai 1:1; 1 Chronicles 3:17-19). The names from Abiud to Jacob appear nowhere else in Scripture, and Matthew does not say where he found them.

decisions.choice: the one called Christ: the one known by the title Christ, the Messiah
decisions.reason: "Called" here introduces the name the reader knows him by, as in 27:17 and 27:22; it casts no doubt on the title. The title means the Anointed One, the king Israel waited for.

decisions.choice: fathered (L); was the father of (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek verb names the father's part in a birth. "Begot" is no longer current English. Balanced and Readable use the phrase people use when they talk about a family tree; Balanced lets later links in a run share one verb ("Isaac of Jacob").

decisions.choice: and of Mary was born Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced names Mary instead of "whom", so that no reader takes "whom" for Joseph.

decisions.choice: Mary was the mother of Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the same pattern of short sentences, and makes plain that Mary, not Joseph, is named as Jesus's parent.

records.source: Πᾶσαι οὖν αἱ γενεαὶ ἀπὸ Ἀβραὰμ ἕως Δαυὶδ γενεαὶ δεκατέσσαρες, καὶ ἀπὸ Δαυὶδ ἕως τῆς μετοικεσίας Βαβυλῶνος γενεαὶ δεκατέσσαρες, καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς μετοικεσίας Βαβυλῶνος ἕως τοῦ χριστοῦ γενεαὶ δεκατέσσαρες.
records.gloss: All therefore the generations from Abraham until David generations fourteen, and from David until the deportation of Babylon generations fourteen, and from the deportation of Babylon until the Christ generations fourteen.
pieces: So there were fourteen generations in all from Abraham to David, fourteen from David to the deportation to Babylon, and fourteen from the deportation to Babylon to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

L.17: So all the generations from Abraham to David [were] fourteen generations, and from David to the deportation to Babylon fourteen generations, and from the deportation to Babylon to the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} fourteen generations.

R.17: So there were fourteen generations from Abraham to David. There were fourteen more from David to the time when the people were taken to Babylon. And there were fourteen more from that time until {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} came.

decisions.choice: fourteen, fourteen, fourteen: a pattern Matthew has arranged, not a full count
alternatives: a complete record of every generation
decisions.reason: To reach fourteen in the second set, Matthew passes over kings (see 1:8 and 1:11). The third set names thirteen men from Shealtiel to Jesus, so either Jechoniah is counted in both sets or Jesus is the fourteenth with Mary's part counted as a generation. The pattern presents the history as ordered by God, from Abraham to David, from David's throne to its loss in the exile, and from the exile to the Messiah.

decisions.choice: fourteen: possibly a play on the name David
decisions.reason: In Hebrew, letters also served as numbers, and the three letters of David's name add up to fourteen. A reader who knew Hebrew could hear David's name in the number. Matthew does not say so, and the suggestion cannot be proved.

decisions.choice: the Christ: the title, the Messiah
decisions.reason: With the article, "the Christ" is the title: the generations lead to the Anointed King.

decisions.choice: until Christ came
decisions.reason: Readable completes the time phrase with a verb, since "until Christ" alone is hard for new readers.

records.source: Τοῦ δὲ Ἰησοῦ χριστοῦ ἡ γένεσις οὕτως ἦν.
records.gloss: Of the then Jesus Christ the origin thus was.
pieces: Now this is how Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} came to be born.

L.18: Now the origin of Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} was like this.

R.18: This is the story of how Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} was born.

decisions.choice: origin: here his birth and how it came about
decisions.reason: This is the word that opens the book in 1:1. There it heads a family line; here it heads the account of how Jesus was conceived and born. The repeated word ties the two sections together: 1:16 left the question how Jesus was born of Mary, and verses 18-25 answer it.

decisions.choice: origin, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: birth, a closely related word found in many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Early manuscripts have the word used in 1:1; many later manuscripts have a word that means only birth. The sense here is much the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: how Jesus came to be born (B); the story of how Jesus was born (R)
alternatives: the birth of Jesus was as follows
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "born", since that is what the account goes on to tell. Literal keeps "origin", the word of 1:1.

records.heading: The birth of Jesus

records.source: μνηστευθείσης τῆς μητρὸς αὐτοῦ Μαρίας τῷ Ἰωσήφ, πρὶν ἢ συνελθεῖν αὐτοὺς εὑρέθη ἐν γαστρὶ ἔχουσα ἐκ πνεύματος ἁγίου.
records.gloss: Having been betrothed the mother of him Mary to the Joseph, before than to come together them she was found in womb having out of Spirit Holy.
pieces: His mother Mary was pledged to be married to Joseph, but before they began to live together it became clear that she was expecting a child through the Holy Spirit.

L.18: When {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother Mary had been pledged to Joseph, before they came together she was found having [a child] in [the] womb from [the] Holy Spirit.

R.18: His mother Mary was engaged to Joseph. But before they started living together, it became clear that she was going to have a baby. The baby was from the Holy Spirit.

decisions.choice: pledged: formally betrothed, a binding agreement that only a divorce could end
alternatives: engaged, in the modern sense of an agreement either side may simply end
decisions.reason: In Jewish custom of the time, betrothal was the first stage of marriage. The couple were legally bound, could be called husband and wife (1:19, 20), and could separate only by divorce. The bride usually stayed in her father's house until the husband took her into his home (1:24).

decisions.choice: came together: began to live together as husband and wife, including sexual union
alternatives: came together in sexual union only
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a couple starting their married life. It includes the husband taking the bride home and their union; 1:25 says plainly that Joseph had no relations with Mary before the birth.

decisions.choice: was found: it became evident that she was pregnant
decisions.reason: The passive "was found" says only that her pregnancy became known. It brings no charge.

decisions.choice: from the Holy Spirit: the child's life began by God's own act, without a human father
alternatives: the Spirit was present at a normal conception
decisions.reason: The narrator tells the reader at once what Joseph does not yet know. The angel repeats it (1:20), and the prophecy of 1:23 and the note in 1:25 rule out Joseph as father.

decisions.choice: she was expecting a child (B); she was going to have a baby (R)
decisions.reason: "Having in the womb" is a Greek way of saying pregnant. Literal keeps the picture; Balanced and Readable use everyday words.

decisions.choice: engaged
decisions.reason: Readable uses the familiar word. Verse 19 then shows that the bond could be ended only by divorce, which the meaning note explains.

records.source: Ἰωσὴφ δὲ ὁ ἀνὴρ αὐτῆς, δίκαιος ὢν καὶ μὴ θέλων αὐτὴν δειγματίσαι, ἐβουλήθη λάθρᾳ ἀπολῦσαι αὐτήν.
records.gloss: Joseph then the husband of her, righteous being and not willing her to expose publicly, purposed secretly to send away her.
pieces: Joseph her husband was a righteous man and did not want to disgrace her in public, so he decided to divorce her privately.

L.19: And Joseph her husband, being righteous and not wanting to make a public example of her, resolved to send her away secretly.

R.19: Joseph, the man she was pledged to, was a man who kept God's law. He did not want to bring shame on her in front of everyone. So he decided to end their marriage quietly.

decisions.choice: righteous: faithful to God's law
decisions.reason: In Matthew a righteous person keeps God's commands (Luke 1:6 uses the word the same way). The law did not let Joseph simply take a wife who seemed to have been unfaithful (Deuteronomy 22:20-21; 24:1).

decisions.choice: being righteous and not wanting: two reasons that together lead to a quiet divorce
alternatives: righteous, and therefore unwilling to shame her
righteous, yet unwilling to shame her
decisions.reason: His faithfulness to the law leads him to end the marriage; his unwillingness to shame her leads him to do it quietly. Some read his righteousness as itself the reason for his mercy. The Greek joins the two with a plain "and".

decisions.choice: send away: divorce
decisions.reason: The verb is the usual word for divorcing a wife (5:31-32; 19:3, 7-9). A betrothal could be ended only by divorce. A quiet divorce needed only a written notice before two witnesses, rather than a public accusation.

decisions.choice: the man she was pledged to, a man who kept God's law
decisions.reason: Readable tells new readers why a man who was not yet living with Mary is called her husband, and what "righteous" means here.

decisions.choice: divorce her (B); end their marriage (R)
decisions.reason: "Send away" might suggest sending her on a journey; Balanced and Readable name what it means.

records.source: ταῦτα δὲ αὐτοῦ ἐνθυμηθέντος ἰδοὺ ἄγγελος κυρίου κατ’ ὄναρ ἐφάνη αὐτῷ λέγων· Ἰωσὴφ υἱὸς Δαυίδ, μὴ φοβηθῇς παραλαβεῖν Μαρίαν τὴν γυναῖκά σου, τὸ γὰρ ἐν αὐτῇ γεννηθὲν ἐκ πνεύματός ἐστιν ἁγίου·
records.gloss: These things then of him having pondered, behold, an angel of Lord in a dream appeared to him saying, Joseph, son of David, not you should fear to take Mary the wife of you, the [thing] for in her having been begotten out of Spirit is Holy.
pieces: While he was turning this over in his mind, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream. "Joseph, son of David," he said, "do not be afraid to take Mary into your home as your wife. The child she has conceived is from the Holy Spirit.

L.20: But as he was considering these things, look, an angel of [the] Lord appeared to him in a dream, saying, "Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary [as] your wife, for what has been conceived in her is from [the] Holy Spirit.

R.20: He was still thinking about this when an angel of the Lord came to him in a dream. The angel said, "Joseph, descendant of David, do not be afraid to take Mary as your wife. Her baby is from the Holy Spirit.

decisions.choice: the Lord: God
decisions.reason: "An angel of the Lord" is the phrase the Greek Old Testament uses for the angel of the Lord God, where the Hebrew has God's name (Genesis 16:7; Judges 13:3). The Lord here is God, as in 1:22.

decisions.choice: having pondered: while he was still weighing what to do
decisions.reason: The verb means to think something over. Joseph has a plan (1:19) but has not acted on it when the angel comes.

decisions.choice: son of David: Joseph is addressed as heir of David's line
decisions.reason: Only Joseph and Jesus are called son of David in Matthew. The angel's words remind Joseph that through him the child will belong to David's family (1:1, 16).

decisions.choice: take Mary as your wife: bring her into his home and complete the marriage
alternatives: marry her for the first time
decisions.reason: They are already pledged (1:18). To take her is the second stage of marriage, when the husband brings the bride home (1:24).

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word (B, R)
decisions.reason: Matthew often uses a word that calls attention to what comes next. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal uses "look". In narrative Balanced and Readable carry its force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: descendant of David
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that Joseph is not David's own son.

decisions.choice: the child she has conceived (B); her baby (R)
alternatives: what has been conceived in her
decisions.reason: The Greek "that which is conceived" is neuter because it speaks of the unborn life. Balanced and Readable say "child" and "baby".

records.source: τέξεται δὲ υἱὸν καὶ καλέσεις τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦν, αὐτὸς γὰρ σώσει τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: She will bear then a son, and you will call the name of him Jesus, he for will save the people of him from the sins of them.
pieces: She will give birth to a son, and you are to name {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} Jesus, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the one who will save {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people from their sins."

L.21: And she will give birth to a son, and you will call {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name Jesus, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will save {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people from their sins."

R.21: She will have a son, and you must give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} the name Jesus, which means 'the Lord saves.' He will save {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people from their sins."

decisions.choice: you will call: a command, you are to name him
alternatives: a prediction of what Joseph will do
decisions.reason: The future tense here gives an instruction, as often in commands from God. In naming the child, Joseph accepts him as his own son (see 1:25).

decisions.choice: Jesus ... for he will save: the name means the Lord saves
alternatives: no connection between the name and the reason
decisions.reason: Jesus is the Greek form of the Hebrew name Joshua, which means "the Lord saves" or "the Lord is salvation". The word "for" ties the name to what he will do; the link is clear in Hebrew but hidden in Greek.

decisions.choice: he: emphatic, he himself, and no other
decisions.reason: The pronoun is written out, which Greek does for emphasis. It is this child who will save.

decisions.choice: save his people from their sins: an echo of Psalm 130:8
alternatives: rescue from enemies or from foreign rule
decisions.reason: Psalm 130:8 says that God will redeem Israel from all its sins. People hoped a messiah would free Israel from its enemies; the angel says this child will free his people from their sins. That work God does is here given to the child.

decisions.choice: which means 'the Lord saves'
alternatives: leave the meaning of the name implicit
decisions.reason: Without the meaning of the name, the "for" makes no sense to a reader who does not know Hebrew. Readable states it inside the angel's words; Balanced and Literal keep "for" and "because", and the meaning note explains the link.

decisions.choice: he is the one who will save
decisions.reason: Balanced brings out the emphatic pronoun.

records.source: τοῦτο δὲ ὅλον γέγονεν ἵνα πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν ὑπὸ κυρίου διὰ τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος·
records.gloss: This then all has happened so that may be fulfilled the [thing] spoken by Lord through the prophet saying,
pieces: All this happened so that the word the Lord had spoken through the prophet would be fulfilled:

L.22: Now all this has happened so that what was spoken by [the] Lord through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying:

R.22: All of this happened to make what the Lord had said through the prophet Isaiah come true. The prophet said:

decisions.choice: the narrator speaks, not the angel
decisions.reason: Verses 22-23 are Matthew's comment on what has happened. This is the first of his "fulfillment" sayings (2:15, 17, 23; 4:14 and others).

decisions.choice: fulfilled: brought to its full meaning and completion
alternatives: only that a prediction came true
decisions.reason: In Matthew the word covers more than prediction. A Scripture is fulfilled when what it spoke of reaches its fullest sense in Jesus. Here it is a promise given to King Ahaz (Isaiah 7:14) that finds its full sense in Jesus's birth.

decisions.choice: spoken by the Lord through the prophet: God is the speaker, the prophet the means
decisions.reason: The two prepositions mark the Lord as the source and the prophet as the one through whom he spoke.

decisions.choice: the prophet Isaiah
decisions.reason: The words quoted in 1:23 are from Isaiah 7:14. Readable names him.

records.source: Ἰδοὺ ἡ παρθένος ἐν γαστρὶ ἕξει καὶ τέξεται υἱόν, καὶ καλέσουσιν τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἐμμανουήλ· ὅ ἐστιν μεθερμηνευόμενον Μεθ’ ἡμῶν ὁ θεός.
records.gloss: Behold, the virgin in womb will have and will bear a son, and they will call the name of him Immanuel, which is being translated With us the God.
pieces: "See, the virgin will become pregnant and have a son, and people will call {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} Immanuel." The name means "God is with us."

L.23: "Look, the virgin will have [a child] in [the] womb and will give birth to a son, and they will call {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name Immanuel," which is translated, "God with us."

R.23: "The virgin will become pregnant and have a son. People will call {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} Immanuel." The name Immanuel means "God is with us."

decisions.choice: the virgin: a woman who has never had sexual relations
decisions.reason: Matthew quotes Isaiah 7:14 in the Greek Old Testament, which uses this word. The Hebrew of Isaiah has a word for a young woman of marriageable age, which does not itself say whether she is a virgin. In Matthew the sense is plain from 1:18, 20 and 25: Mary conceived without a man.

decisions.choice: Isaiah 7:14: the sign given to King Ahaz, read as finding its fullest sense in Jesus
alternatives: a prophecy with no meaning in Isaiah's own day
decisions.reason: In Isaiah the sign was given to Ahaz when enemies threatened Judah (Isaiah 7:1-16). Matthew reads it in the light of Isaiah's later promise of a child who will reign on David's throne (Isaiah 9:6-7).

decisions.choice: they will call: people will call him, an impersonal they
alternatives: you will call (the Greek Old Testament)
decisions.reason: Matthew's wording differs from Isaiah's: not the mother or the king, but people in general will call him Immanuel. Joseph names him Jesus (1:25); Immanuel says who he is.

decisions.choice: God is with us: a name that says what God is doing in this child
alternatives: God with us, as a description of a person who is God
decisions.reason: The name is a short sentence, and Matthew translates it for readers who do not know Hebrew. The book closes with Jesus's promise, "I am with you always" (28:20). Whether the name itself calls Jesus God, or says that God is present among his people in Jesus, the words leave open.

decisions.choice: will become pregnant
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the everyday word for the Greek idiom; Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: people will call him
decisions.reason: "Call his name" is a Hebrew way of saying "name him". "People" makes clear that "they" is no one in particular.

decisions.choice: God is with us
decisions.reason: Hebrew joins "with us" and "God" with no verb, and the words make a sentence. Balanced and Readable supply "is"; Literal keeps the bare phrase.

records.source: ἐγερθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰωσὴφ ἀπὸ τοῦ ὕπνου ἐποίησεν ὡς προσέταξεν αὐτῷ ὁ ἄγγελος κυρίου καὶ παρέλαβεν τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ·
records.gloss: Having been raised then the Joseph from the sleep did as commanded him the angel of Lord and took the wife of him;
pieces: Joseph got up from his sleep and did as the angel of the Lord had commanded him. He took his wife into his home.

L.24: And Joseph, having risen from sleep, did as the angel of [the] Lord had commanded him, and took his wife [to himself].

R.24: Then Joseph woke up. He obeyed the angel of the Lord and took Mary home to be his wife.

decisions.choice: did as the angel commanded: full and immediate obedience
decisions.reason: Matthew uses the same pattern when Joseph obeys again in 2:14 and 2:21. He does what he is told, without a word.

decisions.choice: took his wife: brought her into his home as his wife
alternatives: married her for the first time
decisions.reason: This is the step the angel told him to take (1:20). The betrothal becomes a shared home.

decisions.choice: took Mary home to be his wife
decisions.reason: Readable names Mary and says what taking her meant.

records.source: καὶ οὐκ ἐγίνωσκεν αὐτὴν ἕως οὗ ἔτεκεν υἱόν· καὶ ἐκάλεσεν τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦν.
records.gloss: and not knew her until which she bore a son; and he called the name of him Jesus.
pieces: But he did not have sexual relations with her until she had given birth to a son, and he named {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} Jesus.

L.25: And he did not know her until she had given birth to a son, and he called {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name Jesus.

R.25: But Joseph did not sleep with her until her son was born. And Joseph gave {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} the name Jesus.

decisions.choice: did not know her: had no sexual relations with her
alternatives: did not know her as a person
decisions.reason: "Know" is the Hebrew way of speaking of sexual union, carried into Greek (Genesis 4:1).

decisions.choice: until she bore a son: there was no union before the birth
alternatives: the word implies there was union afterward
decisions.reason: The point is that Joseph had no part in the child's conception or birth. The word "until" by itself neither says nor rules out what followed. Christian traditions differ over Mary's later life; Matthew later names Jesus's brothers and mentions his sisters (13:55-56), and the traditions read those words differently.

decisions.choice: he called his name Jesus: Joseph names him, and so claims him as his son
decisions.reason: Joseph does what the angel told him (1:21). By naming the child he receives him into his family, and Jesus becomes a legal son of David.

decisions.choice: a son, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: her firstborn son, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "her firstborn son", as in Luke 2:7. Early manuscripts have only "a son". Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: did not have sexual relations with her (B); did not sleep with her (R)
decisions.reason: "Know" in this sense is not current English. Balanced uses plain words; Readable uses the everyday expression.

decisions.choice: Joseph
decisions.reason: Readable names Joseph so that "he" is not taken for the child.
